newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude steady to firmer, Dubai bid higher.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude steady to firmer, Dubai bid higher.

text.p: Asian crude prices were steady to firmer on Tuesday and a short squeeze on prompt Dubai sparked aggressive bids on the June/July spread.

The June/July was bid at +20 cents with no offer seen, after being valued on Monday at a notional +3/+10 cents. The rise prompted a sharp narrowing of the Brent/Dubai spread for June to 75/98 cents on Tuesday from a notional $1.10/$1.32 on Monday.
The Dubai June/July spread was in steep contango just last week, the market sources said.
But a flurry of wet deals last week, followed by three cargoes awarded by Indian, soaked up much of the June cargoes.
Traders said the current bids could prompt a seller to emerge as many of last week's deals were done at -10/-8 cents to full-month quotes.
Traders said the sharply narrower Brent/Dubai would also lead to more West African imports, putting further pressure on the already ample supplies of MidEast grades.
Oman traded in line with recent levels. A U.S. major paid MPM -20 cents for a cargo from a Japanese trader, although the deal was a few days old.

News of recent Qatar Marine deals emerged to show the crude traded as low as QGPC -58 cents to a U.S. major. However, the number was achieved prior to the most recent deal at QGPC -45 cents between a Japanese trader and a U.S. major.
Bangchak refinery said it had received several offers of Middle East crude, including up to five offers of Oman on both a Dubai-related and MPM-related basis.
It also received offers for Arab light and medium, Iranian light and heavy and Murban. No Al Shaheem was offered.
The tender is to be awarded later on Tuesday.
